messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired for tenant AtlasCore on dedicated pool atlascore-prod: latency_p99 > 3.5s and 503_rate >= 4% — alert_id=PD-48721 link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-48721

pagerduty: New alert -> PD-48721 (AtlasCore dedicated) — assigned to alex.sre, severity: high

Alex (sre): acked on PD. I'm pulling traces + qps. Seeing spike started ~1765555450. p50 ~120ms, p95 ~800ms, p99 ~3.9s. 503s are originating from proxy backend pool.

Maya (support): Maya here — I just got pinged by AtlasCore SRE contact (Laura). They're seeing degraded responses in prod UI, some customer calls queued. She asked for ETA and whether we can failover to hosted model.

Alex (sre): Noting: reserved capacity for atlascore-prod shows 0 healthy spare nodes (autoscaler prevented scale due to placement constraint). KV cache eviction rate spiked ~+200%. Suspect hot-shard causing IO contention.

Ryan (infra): I'm joining. Running quick checks.

Ops-Bot: Command run by Ryan: ``kubectl -n dedicated-atlascore get pods -l app=proxy -o wide``

Ops-Bot: Output snippet:
```
proxy-0   Running   2/2   10d   10.0.7.12   node-12
proxy-1   Running   2/2   5d    10.0.8.21   node-13
proxy-2   Running   1/2   3h    10.0.9.6    node-22
```

Alex (sre): proxy-2 shows single container restart and elevated cpu. Fetching logs now.

Ops-Bot: Command run by Alex (sre): ``kubectl -n dedicated-atlascore logs proxy-2 -c proxy | tail -n 80``

Ops-Bot: Logs show repeated 502/503 from backend pool: ``upstream read timeout`` and many ``kv-get timeout``.

Alex (sre): Initial mitigation: I'm going to cordon node-22 and move proxy-2 to node-14 to test if node-level IO is culprit. Will also bump allowed burst on autoscaler to permit +2 nodes.

Maya (support): I'll tell Laura: "we have engineers actively investigating, temporary mitigation in progress, ETA ~10-15m; will update in this thread". @Laura (AtlasCore) mentioned they have a weekend spike due to batch import.

pagerduty: PD-48721 acknowledged by Alex (sre) at 1765555562

Ryan (infra): cordoned node-22. Draining proxy-2 -> started eviction. Command: ``kubectl drain node-22 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data``

Ops-Bot: Eviction succeeded; proxy-2 rescheduled to node-14. New pod shows 2/2 ready.

Alex (sre): After reschedule, p99 dropped from 3.9s -> 1.1s, errors down to 0.6%. Still above baseline. Autoscaler still at cap due to placement constraints (affinity). I'm changing pool placement to relax anti-affinity for 10m to allow +2 nodes.

Ryan (infra): Adjusted placement: removed strict anti-affinity for atlascore-prod (10m window). Triggering scale +2.

Ops-Bot: Autoscaler action: scaled atlascore-prod from 6 -> 8 nodes. New nodes joined: node-30, node-31.

Alex (sre): Looks stable — p99 now ~320ms, 503s ~0.2%. KV eviction back to normal. Keeping observer on for 20m.

Maya (support): Updated AtlasCore contact: "We scaled capacity and rescheduled a problematic pod. Latency returning to normal; monitoring for 20m. We'll follow up with post-incident notes".

Alex (sre): Marking incident as mitigated. I'll leave PD alert open until 20m stable window. Creating follow-up ticket: ENG-INC-2026-042 (postmortem + action: remove single-point placement rules, add heat-protection for import windows).

pagerduty: PD-48721 status -> Mitigated by Alex (sre) at 1765555705

Ops-Bot: Suggested follow-ups:
- add alert: reserved_pool_spare_nodes < 1 for >5m
- add runbook step: if kv-get timeout spike -> cordon suspected node + reschedule proxy
- product: coordinate with AtlasCore to throttle import windows or schedule rolling import

Maya (support): I created a customer comms draft and will send to Laura after Alex approves.

Alex (sre): Approved. Please include: brief root cause hypothesis (hot KV shard + placement constraints), mitigation steps taken, and timeline. I'll work with infra to harden autoscaler behavior.

incident-bot: Incident thread closed for PD-48721 — monitoring window completed, status closed.
